newsitem.title: USA: AMR says fee cuts will not hurt earnings.
newsitem.headline: AMR says fee cuts will not hurt earnings.

text.p: AMR Corp said Tuesday its agreement to cut service fees to support Canadian Airlines Corp's restructuring will not materially hurt its earnings.

AMR, the parent of American Airlines, declined to say how much it will cut its fees for computer technology and administrative services. "We have done everything that they have asked of us," said AMR spokesman Al Becker.
Canadian asked AMR for a "large" reduction in fees over four years, Becker said. AMR now gets about $100 million annually from Canadian for its services.
AMR said its agreement to cut its fees and support Canadian's restructuring remains contingent on all parties, including all of Canadian Airlines' unions, supporting the restructuring plan.
While most of Calgary-based Canadian Airlines' unions agreed to support the survival plan, the Canadian Auto Workers remains a major obstacle.
AMR owns a 33 percent economic stake and a 25 percent voting interest in Calgary-based Canadian Airlines.
AMR previously said it may post a charge against its 1996 earnings for the decline in market value of its investment in Canadian Airlines.
